findings.english_quote: The sheep seemed to be living luxuriously and extravagantly.
findings.issue: The simplified wording omits λίαν, the explicit degree modifier attached to the sheep’s extravagant or self-indulgent behavior. “Extravagantly” conveys the behavior but does not separately preserve its emphasized degree.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “The sheep seemed to be living in luxury and behaving very extravagantly.” Review this proposed wording afresh against the complete clause before adopting it.

findings.source_quote: καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ποιμὴν πάνυ ἱλαρὸς ἦν ἐπὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ αὐτοῦ
findings.english_quote: The shepherd was delighted with his flock.
findings.issue: This sentence does not explicitly preserve πάνυ (“very”) or the emphasis of αὐτὸς (“himself”). The subsequent “extremely happy” translates the separate description of his appearance and does not supply these features in this clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider: “The shepherd himself was very happy with his flock.” Review this proposal independently before adoption.

summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against every clause of the supplied working Greek. The standard edition is acceptable. The simplified edition preserves the substantive assertions, conditions, negations, speaker relationships, and contextual repentance language, but loses explicit emphasis in two clauses. The standard’s bracketed “all” remains visibly supplemental; its omission from the simplified edition is not an omission of unbracketed preserved text. This assessment concerns the supplied source and disclosures, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or certification of an exhaustive collation.
